threads.body: [Testing] This compatibility branch is not exercised by any configured test suite. The regular tests use Spring Rabbit 2.1.7 and `version20Test` uses 2.0.1, both of which take the `consumeFromQueue(String)` path; 1.0.0.RELEASE is only the compile-time library. Please add a version-specific integration test against a release without that method that starts a simple listener and verifies Spring, rather than the RabbitMQ wrapper, owns the process span/metrics. Otherwise the newly added legacy behavior can regress while all current tests still pass.

replies.body:
Addressed in 67462083d1717c2cae5eb0aeea15bc5ed6117ea9.

Analysis: Spring Rabbit 1.1.0 does not define BlockingQueueConsumer.consumeFromQueue(String), and its RabbitMQ client is new enough to activate the RabbitMQ wrapper instrumentation. A dedicated suite now starts a SimpleMessageListenerContainer and verifies that Spring emits the consumer process span and metrics while RabbitMQ emits the producer span and no process-duration metric.

Upsides: The test executes the legacy start() advice with both competing instrumentations active and will catch telemetry ownership regressions.

Downsides: The added Testcontainers suite starts another RabbitMQ container during the module check.
